title: QC HAPPENINGS: Tuck Fest, Checkers playoff game, Statesville Wine Walk and more - NewsBreak
text:
By Arri Woodhouse No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago CHARLOTTE ( QUEEN CITY NEWS ) — From family-friendly art exhibitions to outdoor festivals, sports playoffs, and movie nights, many events are happening in Charlotte and the surrounding areas this weekend for people of all ages to enjoy.
FRIDAY, APRIL 24 Hickory Chalk Our Walk
The annual Chalk Our Walk event in Hickory is a family-friendly art exhibition that allows community members of all ages to create chalk art on the sidewalks in front of the Highland Recreation Center. One box of complimentary chalk will be provided with registration.
The two-day event starts at 10 a.m. Visit the website to register .
Twilight 5K at First Ward Park
Come out to First Ward Park for the Twilight 5K. The 3.1-mile trek from the park takes you towards the Elizabeth area and back to a beautiful view of Uptown on 7th Street. The race is preceded by a fun run at 6:15 p.m. before the 5K begins at 6:30 p.m.
Visit the website to register for the race .
Whitewater Center Tuck Fest
The ultimate celebration of the outdoors is back! Tuck Fest at the Whitewater Center features three days of citizen and pro competitions, live music, expos, and action-packed events for everyone to enjoy. The festivities run from Friday through Sunday.
Learn more about the event here .
Rock Hill Annual Come-See-Me Festival
Annual Come-See-Me Festival returns to Rock Hill. Rock Hill’s annual salute to spring is back for ten days full of events and activities. The festival features music, food, and many, many frogs. The festivities conclude on Saturday, April 25, so get out there if you haven’t already to experience the last two days of fun.
There’s something for everybody. Check out the website for full list of events .
Charlotte Checkers Play-Offs
The defending Eastern Conference champs, the Charlotte Checkers, are in the 2026 Calder Cup Playoffs, marking their eighth straight trip to the postseason! The third-seed Checkers will face the sixth-seed Springfield Thunderbirds in the best-of-three first round of the playoffs, and all the matches will take place entirely at Bojangles Coliseum.
The Checkers first game was held on Wednesday, where… Friday’s game starts at 7 p.m. There will also be a game on Saturday if the Checkers win on Friday. Visit website for tickets .
Gastonia Ghost Peppers Opening Weekend Extravaganza
Join the Ghost Peppers for their Opening Weekend Extravaganza at CaroMont Health Park. The team will take on the High Point Rockers at 7 p.m. on Friday and Saturday. But the party isn’t over yet.
On Sunday, April 26, at 1 p.m., come out to the ballpark to celebrate the Ghost Pepper mascot, Peppy’s birthday!
Tickets for the events can be found here .
SATURDAY, APRIL 25 Lake Wylie Run for Life
Support the River Hills Lake Wylie Lions Club for their Run for Life 5K/10K and 1-mile family fun walk. The event takes place in the beautiful lakeside community of River Hills in Lake Wylie at the Camp Thunderbird YMCA. Help the Lions’ cause for children with Type 1 Diabetes and childhood cancer.
The race is $30 per person, $15 for the 1-mile walk. The race starts at 9 a.m. Visit the website for more details .
Repticon in Concord
Repticon, one of the biggest reptile and exotic animal expos in the country, is coming back to Concord. This fun-filled event offers guests the opportunity to learn about animals not normally seen in local pet stores and shop for hundreds of reptiles, amphibians, invertebrates, arachnids, and small exotic animals.
This event, held at the Cabarrus Arena & Events Center, runs from Saturday (9 a.m. to 4 p.m.) thru Sunday (10 a.m. to 4 p.m.). Tickets for both days are $20. To purchase tickets or for more information about the show, please visit the website .
Community Heroes Festival
Calling all Superheroes! Come out to this free family-friendly event that supports two causes: Claire’s Army and The Go Jen Go Foundation . Guests get the opportunity to meet superhero characters, enjoy face painting, games, live music, and local business vendors. Adults, kids (and pups) are encouraged to dress up in superhero costumes.
The event will be held at 215 N. Ames Street in Matthews from noon to 4 p.m. Visit the website to learn more about the event .
QC Culture Film Festival
Celebrate all things cultural and cinematic at the Queen City Culture Film Festival at the Ayrsley Gran Cinema. The event offers a captivating experience that immerses you in the world of film and storytelling. The day-long festival runs from 1 p.m. to 10 p.m.
Visit the website to book your tickets .
Statesville Wine Walk
For the wine lovers, take a stroll to downtown Statesville for the beloved wine walk event. Explore downtown’s shops, restaurants, and businesses while enjoying signature wines. Participating locations will each be assigned a specific wine and attendees will travel from place to place to sample the wines. All wines being sampled will be available for purchase through Wine Maestro.
Tickets for the walk are $35 (if purchased in advance) and $45 on the day of the event (if available). The ticket includes a commemorative wine glass, walking map and wristband. The event runs from 3 p.m. to 7 p.m. Visit website for tickets .
Charlotte Premium Outlets Movies Under the Stars
Grab a chair and your blanket! Charlotte Premium Outlets is hosting a ‘Movies Under the Stars’ event. The free event will include activities, games, and food trucks, located in Parking Field B, across from the entrance of Under Armour and Guess. Saturday night’s screening is Zootopia 2. The event starts at 6 p.m., with the movie starting around 8 p.m.
SUNDAY, APRIL 26 World Ballet Company Swan Lake
World Ballet Company presents Swan Lake, with a live orchestra. The show starts at 6 p.m. at Ovens Auditorium on E. Independence Boulevard in Charlotte.
Tickets for the event range from $75-$152. Visit the website to purchase tickets .
